title: Focus and Focus-Visible Variants
subtopics: Avoiding removal of visible focus without a replacement
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of focus and focus-visible variants.
Apply one appropriate technique to a small Tailwind CSS example.
Verify the expected result and identify a common failure mode.

content.intro: In this lesson, focus on focus and focus-visible variants and connect it to the way Tailwind CSS generates and applies utility styles.
content.why_it_matters: Focus and Focus-Visible Variants matters because interface appearance should reflect actual state while remaining understandable to keyboard, touch and assistive-technology users.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum highlights: Focus styling; Keyboard focus indicators; focus-visible behavior; Accessible focus rings; Avoiding removal of visible focus without a replacement. Treat these as practical decisions rather than a list to memorize: identify the intended behavior, choose the smallest suitable utility or directive, and inspect what the browser receives.

content_blocks.title: Concepts to understand
items: Avoiding removal of visible focus without a replacement

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Focus and Focus-Visible Variants
content_blocks.code:
<button class="rounded-lg bg-blue-700 px-4 py-2 text-white focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-blue-700 motion-reduce:transition-none">
  Save changes
</button>
content_blocks.expected_output: The control has a visible keyboard focus indicator and suppresses nonessential transitions for reduced-motion users.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with the example, change one decision related to focus and focus-visible variants, then compare the outcome. In a Tailwind-enabled project, confirm the generated CSS exists; class strings alone do not make styles available without a configured build.

content_blocks.title: Version and compatibility note
content_blocks.text: This course prioritizes Tailwind CSS v4. Confirm your installed version and use its matching official guide. Snippets using v3 directives or configuration are labelled as legacy and should not be mixed blindly with v4 syntax.

content.task: Create a minimal example demonstrating focus and focus-visible variants. Include a before/after comparison and explain why the chosen utility, variant or directive is appropriate.
task_acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate at least one decision tied to focus and focus-visible variants.
Keep the example easy to inspect, with complete utility names.
Test the outcome and document one limitation or environment assumption.
hints: Identify which listed syllabus topic is most important to focus and focus-visible variants.
Change one utility, token, variant or configuration setting at a time.
Inspect generated CSS and computed styles before changing unrelated code.
content.expected_output: The control has a visible keyboard focus indicator and suppresses nonessential transitions for reduced-motion users.
troubleshooting: If no style appears, verify the package, CSS import and build-tool integration before changing the HTML.
If only a state or breakpoint style fails, check the full class token, source detection, condition and computed CSS.
For a framework snippet, import the stylesheet through its supported entry point and consult the current official guide.
common_mistakes: Applying focus and focus-visible variants without checking generated styles or browser behavior.
Mixing Tailwind v3 and v4 setup examples without a migration plan.
Treating visual appearance as a substitute for semantic markup, keyboard usability or actual component behavior.
summary: Focus and Focus-Visible Variants is one part of a predictable utility-first styling workflow.
Keep examples small, test the built interface and use version-matched documentation.
